caveats: Web research limited: Firecrawl not used, WebFetch hosts (vacuumwars, husqvarna, mammotion, eufy) blocked by sandbox so only search-result snippets were seen; amazon.de not checked. All costs/prices are ASSUMPTION (Low-Medium confidence) unless a source is given. Honest finding: true consumable lock-in is not available to a third party because the robot OEMs own the formats; moats here are registered design/utility model, independent test, or an installer/B2B channel, and are modest (defensibility 2-3).

ideas.name: RoboSill flush ramp threshold profile (B2B flooring/renovation)
ideas.concept: Extruded aluminium door-threshold transition profile with a built-in 6-8 degree robot-friendly ramp and a clip-in silicone insert, sold per door width (80/90 cm) as a permanent, flush alternative to the loose silicone ramps.
ideas.target_customer: Renovators and housing associations/property managers fitting robot-vacuum-friendly floors; flooring installers; private owners with raised sills.
ideas.problem_solved: Robots get stuck on raised thresholds; loose silicone ramps slip, trip people and look cheap. Eufy itself says a ramp only works if the step is just above the robot's climb limit.
ideas.moat_mechanism: EU registered design for the profile (EUR 350 single design per EUIPO fee reform, Boult source) plus a German/Nordic utility model filing (ASSUMPTION EUR 300-600 fees, Low confidence) on the ramp-plus-insert geometry; plus B2B specification relationships with housing associations the founders already know (ex-VELUX building channel) so the profile gets written into renovation specs. Honest limit: a copycat can extrude a similar ramp in weeks outside the design's scope; the real barrier is spec-in at housing associations and installer habit, not IP alone.
ideas.trend_evidence: Robots in 2026 differ in climb height (Vacuum Wars measured MOVA Z60 Ultra 51 mm vs Dreame Aqua10 Ultra Roller 44 mm); many loose ramps sold at roughly USD 13-40 on marketplaces, showing demand but poor products; Eufy/Anker publish ramp guides. Nordic-specific threshold prevalence NOT verified.
ideas.price_point_eur: 29-45 per 90 cm profile (ASSUMPTION, Low); B2B 20-28 at volume
ideas.channel_edge: Founder relationships with housing associations and installers (building industry); Shopify for DIY; low CAC if specified in renovation packages.

ideas.name: Cabinet Bay: recessed robot-vacuum dock insert for standard Nordic cabinet carcasses
ideas.concept: Flat-pack birch-ply and sheet-metal insert that turns a standard base cabinet or hallway unit into a ventilated robot-vacuum bay (dock cut-out, cable passage, open-door sensor clearance, drip tray for mop docks), sized to common mass-market kitchen/wardrobe carcass widths.
ideas.target_customer: Owners of mid-size flats/houses with a self-emptying robot dock they want hidden; housing associations and developers doing kitchen/hall renovations; kitchen installers.
ideas.problem_solved: Docks are bulky and ugly; people DIY hide them in cabinets with heat, access and cable problems. Bosch/Ecovacs launched a built-in cabinet robot in April 2026, validating the 'invisible robot' direction but at a high price and requiring plumbing.
ideas.moat_mechanism: EU registered design (EUR 350) on the insert plus a utility model on the airflow/clearance/drip-tray arrangement (ASSUMPTION EUR 300-600); dimensional fit to specific carcass systems is a switching cost once installers stock it. Honest limit: weak, a joiner can copy in a week; moat is the installer/housing association channel and size-system know-how.
ideas.trend_evidence: Ecovacs, Narwal and Eufy publish 'how to hide a robot vacuum' guides; Bosch+Ecovacs built-in cabinet robot (Apr 2026) shows OEM interest and press coverage.
ideas.channel_edge: Founders' housing association and building-industry contacts for renovation bundles; design-led Shopify/Instagram with before/after content.
ideas.one_off_tooling_eur: 1,000-2,500 laser/CNC jigs and sheet-metal dies plus ~700 IP (ASSUMPTION, Low)

ideas.name: Independently lab-tested H13 filter + brush annual service kits for the top Nordic robot models
ideas.concept: Annual maintenance kits (2 filters, side brushes, pad set) for 4-5 best-selling robot vacuums, with each filter carrying a published independent particle-retention test report and a registered 'tested' mark.
ideas.target_customer: Allergy-aware robot-vacuum owners and pet households who currently buy unbranded marketplace filters.
ideas.problem_solved: Aftermarket 'HEPA' filters are unregulated and often misfit or underperform; reviewers report wrong sizes and filters that failed a fog test.
ideas.moat_mechanism: Independent lab report per filter type (ASSUMPTION EUR 1,500-3,000 per type at an accredited lab, Low confidence; not verified) plus EU trademark (~EUR 850 for one class, ASSUMPTION) and exact-fit tooling data per model; competitors must pay the same test to claim parity. Honest limit: the category is full of cheap private-label kits and OEM kits (Dreame sells its own kit); a copycat can test too. Likely close to the 'dominated by private label' kill, so score low.
ideas.trend_evidence: Vacuum Wars tested bestselling Amazon 'HEPA' filters for Roborock Q7 and reports most failed (single-outlet test); RTINGS says third-party filters vary; fit complaints in third-party kit reviews; OEM kits at Dreame store show OEM competes directly.
ideas.channel_edge: Nilfisk/robotics sourcing contacts for filter media and tested spec; Amazon EU with test-report A+ content; repeat purchase via annual reminder email.
ideas.est_first_order_eur: 6,000-9,500 incl. test fees for 2 filter types and 400-500 kits
ideas.one_off_tooling_eur: 0-1,500 (die-cut tools for filters); test fees counted in first order

ideas.name: Robot-mower wash stand with brush-pad refills (hose-fed, drains to ground)
ideas.concept: Folding steel stand that cradles a robot mower upright, with a low-flow hose ring and replaceable brush/sponge pads that sit over the blade disk and wheels, so the mower can be cleaned in 2 minutes without tipping it. Sold universal with model-specific cradle inserts.
ideas.target_customer: Swedish and Danish owners of Husqvarna/Gardena/Mammotion/Dreame mowers, especially in clay or wet soil; mower installers/dealers.
ideas.problem_solved: OEM guidance requires cleaning, but some makers say hose-washing is allowed only for some models and warn never to use a pressure washer, while others (Stihl) say never use a hose; a stand with controlled low-flow and brushes gives a safe routine.
ideas.moat_mechanism: EU registered design (EUR 350) plus utility model on cradle-plus-brush-pad interface (ASSUMPTION EUR 300-600) and proprietary brush-pad format as consumable refill (EUR 9-12 per pair). Honest limit: Mammotion already sells a cleaning stand at GBP 69, so this is not first; moat is only the refill format and model inserts; a copycat can copy within months. Defensibility 2-3.
ideas.trend_evidence: Nordic retailer Elkjop reported nine times more robot mowers sold than the previous year (undated); Sweden robotic mower market about USD 65m in 2025 (paid report, Medium-Low); Husqvarna has cleaning kit and wheel brush refills, proving a consumable market exists.
ideas.channel_edge: Robotics sourcing network for stamped steel and brush supplier; garden/mower dealers as B2B; Shopify seasonal (spring) TikTok demo content.

ideas.name: Anti-tangle comb roller upgrade for top-selling robots
ideas.concept: Drop-in replacement main roller with a replaceable comb-blade insert and spiral bristle layout for 3-4 popular models, sold with spare comb inserts as consumable.
ideas.target_customer: Long-haired pet and hair households whose OEM roller tangles.
ideas.problem_solved: Hair wrap on rollers causes motor strain and manual scissors cleaning; users ask for better aftermarket rollers.
ideas.moat_mechanism: Utility model / patent on comb-insert geometry (ASSUMPTION EUR 600-1,500 national/EUR; patent EUR 5k+ is a kill, so utility model only) and registered design; honest limit: OEMs already ship anti-tangle rollers (Dreame, Ecovacs, Eufy) so market is shrinking for new machines; infringement risk from OEM patents is unchecked and must be cleared by an FTO search before any order.
ideas.trend_evidence: Wyze forum user says they would buy an aftermarket better roller; OEM anti-tangle marketing everywhere; unbranded replacement rollers sold at around USD 30.
ideas.channel_edge: Nilfisk/robotics sourcing contacts for brush maker; Amazon EU fit-finder listings.
ideas.one_off_tooling_eur: 2,500-4,500 injection/extrusion tooling plus IP (ASSUMPTION, Low); high risk

ideas.name: Dock-tank descaler and pad-wash tablets for self-washing robot mop docks
ideas.concept: Effervescent citric/surfactant tablets dosed for 3-4 L robot mop dock tanks, sold in 3-month and 12-month packs, with a hard-water (Nordic region) variant.
ideas.target_customer: Owners of self-washing mop docks who face limescale and odour in pads and tanks.
ideas.problem_solved: Dock tanks and pads get smelly or limescaled; OEMs sell their own solution at high price.
ideas.moat_mechanism: Trade-secret formulation through a contract formulator with exclusivity clause (ASSUMPTION EUR 0 upfront but MOQ) and a safety-data-sheet/CLP compliance file (ASSUMPTION EUR 500-1,000). Honest limit: this is weak, as copycats can reverse engineer a citric tablet quickly; OEM warranty compatibility must be confirmed with each brand. Lock-in is only habit. Defensibility 2.
ideas.trend_evidence: Third-party consumables sit next to OEM ones on retailer pages for Dreame/Roborock; no direct demand data for tablets was found. UNVERIFIED.
ideas.channel_edge: Cleaning-chemistry sourcing from Nilfisk network; subscription via Shopify; low fulfilment weight.

ideas.name: Reusable washable mop-pad system with own hook-plate format and wash-bag
ideas.concept: A branded family of washable microfibre pads on a stick-on universal adapter plate, plus mesh wash-bag, sized for the 3 most common round/oval mop docks; replacement pads sold in 4-packs.
ideas.target_customer: Owners of mop robots who dislike the OEM price of pads and landfill from disposable ones.
ideas.problem_solved: OEM pads are pricey (OEM stores sell multi-pad kits) and third-party pads are mixed in fit; a durable pad set with a fit guarantee fits the repeat-purchase model.
ideas.moat_mechanism: Registered design for the adapter-plate-plus-pad (EUR 350) and a trademark; honest limit: OEM pad/plate formats are likely protected by patents and designs, so a freedom-to-operate check is mandatory and adapter use may void warranties; copycat Chinese sellers already sell compatible pads (Plutoos, JETtools). Defensibility 1-2; included for completeness, expect a kill.
ideas.trend_evidence: Many compatible pad listings exist for Roborock, Dreame and MOVA models; fit complaints appear in buyer reviews.
ideas.channel_edge: Amazon EU variation listings; sourcing from robotics supply chain.
ideas.one_off_tooling_eur: 500-1,500 die-cut and adapter mould plus IP
